programmes.d: Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon head from Skipton to Liverpool for their final auction showdown.
David Barby's after something quirky, while David Harper's going for the killer deal as they shop from Aberystwyth to the auction in Shrewsbury.
Can a salt glazed Toby jug reign supreme over a brass dancing figure at auction?
It's day one for expert Thomas Plant and Road Trip newbie, Scottish auctioneer Paul Laidlaw, as they travel from Skipton to Sheffield.
The conclusion of David Barby and David Harper's epic tour begins in Hereford--but who will be crowned king at the auction in Llanelli?
A Chinese ink drawing of pigs has one expert hoping to bring home the bacon.
Day two for dynamic duo Thomas Plant and Paul Laidlaw sees them attempt to outwit each other on their way from Bolsover to the auction in Stamford.
Antique aficionados Margie Cooper and Mark Hill take in the sights of Yorkshire behind the wheel of an MGB Roadster, splashing their cash on hidden gems to take to auction.
One expert needs a stroke of luck with a large handsaw and bronze boat propeller.
It's charm versus mathematical prowess, as experts Thomas Plant and Paul Laidlaw hit the shops between Huntingdon and Towcester.
Big hopes that a piece of a nearly 1000-year-old building will secure a final auction win.
Glass lover Mark Hill and silver specialist Margie Cooper go head-to-head in a 1980 MGB Roadster, searching for antiques across the Yorkshire coast, from Bridlington to Pickering.
Thomas Plant and Paul Laidlaw's negotiating tactics are tested to the limit as they travel from Olney to the auction in Watlington.
It’s a vintage fairground mallet versus an Art Deco French gilded mantel clock.
Glass lover Mark Hill and silver specialist Margie Cooper continue their head-to-head in a 1980 MGB Roadster, hunting for antiques in Yorkshire, from Darlington to Barnard Castle.
Thomas Plant and Paul Laidlaw spend their final day of antique adventuring heading from Tetsworth to the final auction showdown in Pewsey.
Finds include vintage good luck charms and an Inuit stone carving.
In an MGB Roadster, glass champion Mark Hill and silver lover Margie Cooper hunt for antiques around the border towns of Scotland and England, from Berwick-upon-Tweed to Hawick.
It's Charlie Ross and Charles Hanson's first day together as they kick off their journey in Bridlington and head to an auction showdown in Doncaster.
Finds include a vintage artists palette, Arabic coffee pot, and a cooper plaque.
Charlie Ross and Charles Hanson are getting on famously as they drive the second leg of their road trip from Scunthorpe to Grantham.
Can silver lover Margie Cooper make it a clean sweep as she and 20th century design expert Mark Hill head for the heart of Edinburgh in a 1980 MGB Roadster?
Can a fighter jet gear box help Ishy Khan win this leg of the road trip?
The competition heats up on day three as the two Charlies journey from King's Lynn to the auction in Beccles.

It's a tale of three countries as good chums Natasha Raskin Sharp and James Braxton take in Wales, England and Scotland. Finds include a hat that isn't a hat, Victorian pottery, an interesting shop sign a dolphin in need of a dip and more.
Final finds include a French mantel clock and Chinese bellows.
It's day four of Charlie Ross and Charles Hanson's road trip, heading from Lavenham in Suffolk to Greenwich--until their car breaks down.

Natasha Raskin Sharp and James Braxton journey from Pontypridd to Monmouth. Natasha picks up a pair of 19th century lusters, which she hopes will do the business at auction, while James takes a punt with a tin plate toy horse.
Silver spoons and a Victorian Egyptian fob bring drama to the saleroom!
The fifth leg of the journey for Charles Hanson and Charlie Ross takes them from Royal Tunbridge Wells to Rye in East Sussex for a final showdown.

Natasha Raskin Sharp and James Braxton are in the Black Country. James finds an enormous specimen of a rather famous bird and a noisy antique. Natasha gets her hands on a rather macabre little curio and goes gaga for some ceramics.
Margie and Tim discover Tai Chi in Liverpool before their auction battle commences.
It's a new chapter as we hit the road with seasoned auctioneers James Braxton and Jonathan Pratt as they travel from Altrincham to Nantwich.
Can 100-year-old recipe books cook up a win for one expert at auction?

Natasha Raskin Sharp and James Braxton head to Lancashire and the Lake District. Natasha eyes some more brooches. James takes a fancy to some sizable and suitably heavy items, but a big spend leaves him a little light in the pocket.
James Braxton and Jonathan Pratt search for bargains while traveling from Leek in Staffordshire to Birmingham.
Seagull attack caught on camera! But who will steal an auction win?

Scotland is Natasha Raskin Sharp and James Braxton's final stop. James is drawn to big and colorful items, while Natasha has an eye for the unusual, with one item conjuring up a memory of her grandfather and another reminding her of James.
James Braxton and Jonathan Pratt are determined to up their game as they head from Stratford upon Avon to the auction in Frome, Somerset.
Psychic sketches and an obelisk turn up at Margie and Tim’s final auction slamdown.
It's day four of James Braxton and Jonathan Pratt's road trip as they scour local antique shops between Wells and the auction in Crewkerne.

Hettie Jago and Tim Medhurst have a replica Jaguar for their shopping trip which begins in sunny Sussex. Tim uncovers an unusual teapot, possibly by William Hutton. Hettie's interest is piqued by an Art Deco figurine of a mouse.
Raj and Hettie’s first outing, featuring the opportunity of a lifetime!
James Braxton and Jonathan Pratt's fifth leg takes them from Crewkerne in Somerset to Lostwithiel in Cornwall for their final auction showdown.

Deep into Surrey, England's most wooded county, Tim Medhurst buys a plaster bust and some salt glazed Toby jugs. Hettie Jago, meanwhile, picks up an Italian gilt box and an elegant brass dancing figure.
Raj and Hettie get dazzled by jewels in Norfolk.
It's a brand-new week, hitting the road with David Barby and David Harper as they travel all the way from Moy to Omagh in Northern Ireland.

Hettie Jago and Tim Medhurst begin today's journey in Henley-on-Thames Hettie finds a fairground carousel horse and an early 20th century Chinese ink drawing of some pigs. Tim buys a granite mortar and a GPO clock with his name on it.
Wooden stilts, Derbyshire Blue John and the shocking story of the Witch Finder General!
David Barby and David Harper grapple with Euros as they travel from Athlone to Kells in Ireland.
Art deco penguin cocktail shaker vs. a soapstone Inuit carving!
Hettie Jago and Tim Medhurst start out in Lyndhurst. Hettie picks up a large hand saw and a bronze three blade boat propeller. Tim buys an unusual nut with nautical interest and a very special coin.
David Barby and David Harper have crossed the North Sea to Wales--and now the competition heats up as they travel from Prestatyn to Criccieth.
An anatomical eye model and old rugby ball go head-to-head in this final auction.

It's the last hurrah for Hettie Jago and Tim Medhurst. Hettie spends big on a piece of jewelry that she hopes will give her the big win. Tim buys a slice of a nearly 1000-year-old building and a very interesting treen box.
David Barby's after something quirky, while David Harper's going for the killer deal as they shop from Aberystwyth to the auction in Shrewsbury.
Flamboyant besties Roo and Mark go head-to-head in Yorkshire.

In the Kent countryside, Irita Marriott and Ishy Khan kick off their road trip in a 1971 Sunbeam Rapier. Ishy finds a vintage fairground mallet while Irita is entranced by an Art Deco French gilded mantel clock.
The conclusion of David Barby and David Harper's epic tour begins in Hereford--but who will be crowned king at the auction in Llanelli?
Mark takes on Roo and swoons over a rare find.

Traveling along the Kent coast in their 1971 Sunbeam Rapier, Ishy Khan uncovers some vintage good luck charms while Irita Marriott uncovers an Inuit stone carving and an antique compass encased in walnut.
Charles Hanson and David Barby kick off their journey in Lichfield, Staffordshire, and head for an auction showdown in Coventry.
A car-shaped teapot and art nouveau vase race to auction, but who will ring in profits?
It's game on as Charles Hanson and David Barby travel from Malvern to a head-to-head auction in Pewsey Wiltshire.

In Suffolk, Irita Marriott unearths a vintage metal artist's palette and Ishy Khan is inspired to find his own metal. They discover an Arabic coffee pot, a brass bowl and a cooper plaque, which may be highly sought after Newlyn copper.
Will Mark’s rare piece of glass beat Roo at auction?
Its day three for Charles Hanson and David Barby as they battle it out from Ross on Wye, Herefordshire, to Frome in Somerset for the auction.

Irita Marriott falls in love with an early 20th century Islamic bowl, vintage fountain pens and a vintage steamer suitcase, while Ishy Khan takes his chances on a Victorian brooch, an Art Deco coin purse and a gear box from a jet fighter.
Can a glass dog beat a lion head in this final auction of the trip?
It's all to play for as Charles Hanson and David Barby travel from Chester in Cheshire hunting antiques for the showdown in North Rode near Congleton.
Our jewelry experts go awol with a wooden donkey block and fairy money box!

It's the final day of the road trip! Irita Marriott finds a 19th century French mantel clock, a vintage ink standish and a copper jug. Ishy uncovers a Chinese bellows, vintage glass salt dish and an early 20th century inkwell.
It's neck and neck between Charles Hanson and David Barby on the last leg of their journey from Stafford to Nottingham for the final showdown.
Ishy may have found the world’s biggest pencil, but will anyone buy it?
On this first leg Anita Manning and James Lewis start out in Deddington, Oxfordshire, then cross into Hertfordshire for auction in St Albans.
Newcomer Margie Cooper battles it out with veteran Mark Stacey, starting the week in Chilham, Kent, and ending at auction in Heathfield, East Sussex.
Lobsters, lizards and a silver duck are discovered deep in Gloucestershire!
Anita Manning and James Lewis head to the London district of Wimbledon, travel through Molesey in Surrey then to auction near Alresford in Hampshire.
It couldn't be closer as Margie Cooper and Mark Stacey go hunting that antique gem, from Rochester in Kent to a showdown in Colchester in Essex.
Catherine and Ishy get their hands on centuries old plasticine!
Anita Manning and James Lewis begin near Lacock in Wiltshire, then visit Bath, Frome and Swindon en route to auction in Cirencester, Gloucestershire.
